title: Egg omelet or scrambled egg with meat and dark‑green vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of eggs prepared as an omelet or scrambled, combined with lean meat (such as chicken breast or turkey) and dark‑green vegetables (spinach, broccoli, kale). Eggs provide high‑quality protein, while the vegetables are rich in vitamins, minerals and antioxidants.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggs contain all essential amino acids needed by the human body.
Dark‑green vegetables like spinach provide over 20% of the daily value of vitamin K.
Poultry meat is one of the leanest sources of animal protein, low in saturated fat.
Cooking eggs as an omelet retains more nutrients compared with prolonged frying.
The combination of protein and vegetables enhances iron absorption from the meat.

items.title: Complete high‑quality protein
items.content: Eggs and meat supply all essential amino acids, supporting tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and meat provide vitamin B12, while dark‑green vegetables are a good source of folate (B9), important for nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Spinach and broccoli contain lutein, zeaxanthin and vitamin C, which help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Bone support
items.content: Vitamin K and calcium from the greens contribute to bone mineralization.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Choosing lean meat and using minimal oil makes the dish suitable for heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg white proteins.

items.title: Improperly cooked meat
items.content: Undercooked poultry can harbor harmful bacteria; ensure thorough cooking.

items.title: Oxalates in greens
items.content: Large amounts of spinach can increase oxalate intake, which may be problematic for people prone to kidney stones.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: While eggs are nutritious, people with high cholesterol should monitor portion size.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Beat the eggs, add diced lean meat and pre‑cooked or lightly sautéed dark‑green vegetables. Cook in a non‑stick pan with a small amount of olive oil, stirring until the desired consistency is reached. Season with pepper, paprika, or fresh herbs as desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: The dish is best enjoyed fresh. If needed, store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Reheat in a pan or microwave, adding a little oil to prevent drying out.
